scene_name: Staffing bottleneck with sufficient raw material and two already-built small lines
scene_goal: Validate whether the agent can diagnose staffing bottleneck when committed demand already exists across several seeded markets, suppliers are available, raw material remains sufficient, cash is healthy, two small lines already exist, and the only remaining production worker is already occupied by an in-progress plan.

day3: the seeded markets already exist and the first pilot orders have already been accepted
the second small line is already available
the company no longer looks like a cold start
both physical lines can already be exercised before any staffing shock is introduced
day5: the short pilot plan and the cross-line secondary pilot have already completed
both lines have already produced real output
the company now looks like a live operation with validated demand rather than a cold start
day7: multiple future-dated accepted orders already exist
the second line is still physically available
the staffing shock has just reduced production to one remaining worker
day10: analysis should identify a staffing-rooted primary contradiction; acceptable observable labels are staff_shortage or production_capacity_bottleneck when HR is still the lead correction channel and procurement is not acting first
hr should be the lead department
the preferred first action should be handle_recruitment for production
production should not be the lead responder with build_production_line because line count already exists
procurement should not be the lead responder because raw material remains sufficient
sales should not be the lead responder because committed demand already exists
day20: recruitment or equivalent workforce recovery should have happened
the idle second line should begin contributing to output
accepted backlog should begin moving toward completed orders
the system should avoid replacing a staffing bottleneck with unnecessary procurement or market expansion

evidence_focus: whether day10 analysis identifies a staffing-rooted primary contradiction rather than drifting back to market or procurement problems
whether day10 hr_action expresses handle_recruitment intent immediately after takeover
whether day10 production_action avoids treating build_production_line as the first fix

whether day10 snapshot shows five active markets, two available small lines, sufficient raw material, meaningful but insufficient finished-goods coverage, and one occupied remaining production worker together
whether day20 accepted orders start converting into completed orders after headcount recovery
